description:
Advances: specled.api_boundary, specled.binding

canonicalize_head/1 emits structurally different envelopes per resolution path (BEAM 4-tuple over all clauses vs source-fallback 5-tuple over the first def clause), so the same unchanged function hashes two ways and a cold tree fabricates plausible-looking realization drift.

api_boundary entries record resolved_via (beam|source); the detector compares same-path only and emits branch_guard_resolution_path_divergence (warning) on labeled cross-path encounters. Unlabeled legacy entries keep legacy drift semantics — "assume beam" was refuted on this repo own corpus: private-function bindings always resolve via source, so their unlabeled baselines were source-written. Divergence blocks baseline refresh in both branches (including --accept-drift) and excludes the pair from attestations. No hasher_version bump: same-path hashes unchanged.

Test-harness fidelity fallout: Mix test task disables :debug_info for runtime compilation, so every runtime-compiled fixture had been resolving via the source fallback — the suite never exercised the beam path production uses. Fixtures now compile via SpecLedEx.FixtureCompiler with debug_info forced on; the stripped-debug fixture deliberately compiles without it. make test gains TEST= passthrough.

ADR: specled.decision.resolution_path_provenance
title: Resolution-path provenance: cross-path hash comparison is divergence, not drift
